title: Bar Tamlon
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Pesikta Rabbati, the second section on the Ten Commandments, subsection 6, relates that a man deposited money with Bar Tamlon, who denied receiving it. They came to court, and Bar Tamlon had to swear. He put the money inside a hollow cane and handed the cane to the depositor to hold while he swore, etc. Nedarim 25a tells the well-known story of Rava’s cane, but does not name the man.

notes.text: Bar Tamlon is the person denying the deposit and taking the oath. The depositor holds the cane containing his money. The Bavli’s analogous story is about an unnamed borrower; it does not name Bar Tamlon.

The consulted Pesikta Rabbati 22 cane story names Bar Talmyon (בר תלמיון), while Hyman writes Bar Tamlon (בר תמלון). Hyman’s exact subsection-6 numbering scheme remains unverified. The unnamed Bavli borrower is not thereby identified.
